cases.label: Tags: values differing only in case both match a case-insensitive search and keep their own case in the result
cases.reasoning: T-SQL LIKE under the CI_AS collation is case-insensitive, so searching 'ab' matches Tags 'ab' and 'AB'; the conversion uses ~* (case-insensitive regex). Both rows are ordered by distinct names; the JSON must list both.

cases.label: Tags: two matching rows share the same Tags value (a non-key tie); both are returned in name order
cases.reasoning: Rows 1 and 3 share Tags = 'dup' (a non-key value) and both match the search; their StockItemNames differ, so the Windows-collation ORDER BY is deterministic and both must appear on each engine.

cases.label: Tags: a trailing space in the data is matched by LIKE '%x%'
cases.reasoning: Tags 'abc ' ends in a space; LIKE N'%abc%' matches it on SQL Server and the translated regex matches it too. A conversion that rtrimmed the column would still match here, but the stored/compared value must keep the space.

cases.label: Tags: character class [a-c] matches one of a, b, c (T-SQL LIKE, not PostgreSQL LIKE)
cases.reasoning: T-SQL LIKE treats [a-c] as a character class; PostgreSQL LIKE does not, so the conversion must translate it to a regex class. 'b' matches, 'd' does not, 'x[a-c]' does not (literal class only when escaped).

cases.label: Tags: a backslash is an ordinary character in T-SQL LIKE (no escape)
cases.reasoning: T-SQL LIKE has no escape character, so 'a\b' matches the literal 'a\b'; PostgreSQL LIKE would treat backslash specially, so the translation must emit a literal backslash in the regex.

cases.label: Tags: TOP(@MaximumRowsToReturn) returns exactly two of five hits, ordered by the Windows collation
cases.reasoning: Five rows match; @MaximumRowsToReturn = 2 returns the first two in Latin1_General_100_CI_AS order (LIMIT 2 in the conversion, same ordering collation). StockItemIDs 1,3,5,7,9 (gaps) confirm the key is by value, and the two-row limit must agree.

cases.label: Tags: no row qualifies, so FOR JSON ... ROOT returns an empty string, not an empty array
cases.reasoning: When nothing matches, FOR JSON AUTO with ROOT yields '' on SQL Server (not {"StockItems":[]}); the conversion returns '' via the count(*) = 0 branch. Both must produce the empty document.

cases.label: Tags: NULL versus '' — a NULL Tags never matches, an empty Tags matches only '%%'
cases.reasoning: Tags is nullable: a NULL value makes LIKE NULL (no match) on both engines, while '' matches the search '' (pattern '%%'). Searching '' with one NULL row and one '' row distinguishes NULL from ''.
